audit_result.proof_trace: The function reads the last attendance type with a plain SELECT (no FOR UPDATE, no advisory lock) then inserts without an ON CONFLICT guard or UNIQUE constraint on (user_id, timestamp/date/type). Under PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED, two concurrent transactions both read the same last_type before either commits, compute the same v_new_type, and both INSERT successfully — producing duplicate attendance records of the same type. No serialization mechanism exists at any layer: the attendances table has only non-unique indexes, the function holds no row-level or advisory lock, and the anon-callable RPC endpoint (GRANT EXECUTE TO anon per migration 20260317000001) is reachable directly without going through the client-side 'processing' state guard.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An NFC reader malfunction or an attacker sends two rapid anon RPC calls to `attendance.record_attendance_by_card` with the same card_id; both transactions read NULL (or the same last record) before either commits, both compute the same v_new_type ('in' or 'out'), and both INSERTs succeed — corrupting the user's in/out state machine with a duplicate record.

PROP-0000-create-inv-019.text: Concurrent card swipes must not create duplicate attendance records (race condition).
PROP-0000-create-inv-019.assertion: forall c, t: concurrent_calls(record_attendance_by_card, c) => serialized_insert(c) (no duplicate timestamp+user)
